newsitem.title: USA: U.S. propane prices soar on cold weather, demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. propane prices soar on cold weather, demand.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices soared on Tuesday in midday trade seen brisk mostly in the Midwest, which has been hit by cold weather and strong crop drying demand, players said.
"It seems like every buyer is out here today," said one Midwest trader. "The weather is cold and people are still bringing grain in hot and heavy, and it's wet."
Propane is used as fuel for drying corn and some grain crops before being brought to market or storage.
In Conway, Kansas, hub spot propane jumped 1.25 cents to between 54.50 cents and 54.75 cents a gallon.
Traders said 54.75 cents and 55.00 cents were sold.

In Mont Belvieu, Texas, spot propane edged up a half cent to 52.75/53.00 cents with 52.75 cent sold. Traders said much of the focus in Belvieu was on ethane purity, which was up 2.25 cents on strong chemical demand.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
